prompts.display_text: Pin a country that Saints names as having a Church Family Services agency in the 2000s.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 35: LDS Family Services ran agencies in only these countries in the 2000s. Pin one.
prompts.summary: In the 2000s LDS Family Services ran agencies in only six countries: the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain and Japan. Japan was the only Asian country on the list.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Home base of the agency.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: One of six countries with agencies.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: One of six countries with agencies.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Listed as Great Britain.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: One of six countries with agencies.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: The only Asian country with an agency.

prompts.display_text: Pin a South Pacific country or territory President David O. McKay visited on his 1955 tour.
prompts.text_original: In January and February 1955, David O. McKay became the first Church president to tour the South Pacific missions, choosing a temple site in New Zealand along the way. Pin a South Pacific country or territory he visited on that tour.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies; Church newsroom; Ensign Dec. 1998
prompts.note: Hawaii is in the North Pacific and is not scored.
prompts.summary: Early in 1955, President David O. McKay and his wife, Emma Ray, flew through the South Pacific, meeting Saints in Fiji, Tonga, both Samoas, the Cook Islands and Tahiti before visiting New Zealand and Australia. In New Zealand he quietly chose the hill near Hamilton where the first temple in the Southern Hemisphere would rise.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: First Church president to visit Australia, 1955.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Visited the Hamilton college project and chose the temple site; announced Feb. 17, 1955.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Visited Tongatapu and Vava'u and spoke of a future temple.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: Met Saints in Pesega and Sauniatu, January 14-17, 1955.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Met Saints in Pago Pago and Mapusaga, January 14, 1955.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Spoke to Saints in Suva, January 9, 1955.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: First Church president to visit Tahiti, January 18-20, 1955.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Held a one-hour meeting with 66 members at Aitutaki while his plane refueled.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology names a woman who translated the Book of Mormon
prompts.text_original: A country or territory whose Global Histories chronology names a woman as a translator of the Book of Mormon, in whole or in part, into a local language
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Albania, Thailand, Ghana, Bulgaria, Iceland, Guam, Zimbabwe
prompts.note: Scoped to the Global Histories chronologies read 27 Oct 2026; women have translated scripture in many other languages too.
prompts.summary: Local members, many of them women, have carried much of the work of translating the Book of Mormon. Church chronologies name Evangeline Coy for Bulgarian, Srilaksana Suntarahut for Thai, Sveinbjorg Gudmundsdottir for Icelandic, Maria Salas Calvo for CHamoru, Priscilla Sampson-Davis for Fante and two lead translators for Albanian.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: Brikena Ribaj and Juventila Sinamati were lead translators of the Albanian edition of 1999.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Srilaksana Suntarahut joined the review committee in 1970 and was principal translator of the 1976 Thai edition.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Evangeline Kokotanova Coy, a convert in the United States, finished the first Bulgarian manuscript in 1934.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Priscilla Sampson-Davis began translating hymns into Fante in 1980 and later translated the Book of Mormon.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: Maria Salas Calvo translated the CHamoru selections issued in book form in 1989.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Sveinbjorg Gudmundsdottir and Halldor Hansen translated the Icelandic edition published in 1981.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Dorothy Tembo was on the team whose Shona triple combination, Book of Mormon included, came out in 2007.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American or Caribbean country or territory where a current General Authority Seventy was born (October 2026).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies were born in Latin America or the Caribbean. Pin a country or territory in that region where a current General Authority Seventy was born, according to the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.note: Elder Perkins was born in Colorado and Elder Valenzuela in Mexico, so neither adds a country.
prompts.summary: The Church's General Authority Seventies come from many nations. As of October 2026 their official biographies list birthplaces across Latin America and the Caribbean, from Brazil and Mexico to Jamaica, Venezuela and Puerto Rico. Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Chile each have several.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Elders Aidukaitis, Godoy, Silva, Farias and others were born in Brazil.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Elders Alonso (Mexico City), Casillas (Tijuana), Villanueva (Oaxaca), Roman (Iguala).

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Elders Walker and Alliaud (Buenos Aires), Ortega, Costa.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Elders Giuffra and Villar (Valparaiso), Gimenez (Antofagasta), Vargas (Puerto Varas).

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Elder Valeri V. Cordon, born in Guatemala City.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Elder Taylor G. Godoy, born in Lima.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Elder Mathias Held, born in Bogota.

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: Elders Hugo E. Martinez (Mayaguez) and Jorge M. Alvarado (Ponce).

answers.name: Venezuela
answers.fact: Elder Pedro X. Larreal, born in Valencia.

answers.name: Jamaica
answers.fact: Elder Kevin G. Brown, born in Manchester, Jamaica.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where a current General Authority Seventy was born (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies were born in Africa. Pin an African country where a current General Authority Seventy was born, according to the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, seven African nations are birthplaces of current General Authority Seventies, including Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Botswana. Elder Edward Dube of Zimbabwe serves in the Presidency of the Seventy.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Elder Isaac K. Morrison, born in Takoradi.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Elders Ojediran (Ibadan), Chigbundu (Ahiaba Okpuala) and Egbo (Port Harcourt).

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Elder Thabo Lebethoa, born in Soweto.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Elders Alfred Kyungu and Thierry K. Mutombo (Kinshasa).

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Elder Edward Dube of the Presidency of the Seventy, born in Chirumhanzu.

answers.name: Ivory Coast
answers.fact: Elder D. Martin Goury, born in Gagnoa, Cote d'Ivoire.

answers.name: Botswana
answers.fact: Elder Clement M. Matswagothata, born in Middlepits.
